purpose: Change an Account's canonical primary email only after explicit confirmation of the new mailbox and a guarded, durable Identity apply transaction.

implementation_revision.semantics: WELL-17 email-change lifecycle plus WELL-18's development/test-only, flag-controlled current Privacy proof read immediately before mutation; it adds no production purpose-consent requirement.

collaborating_domains.ownership: Owns the durable delivery intent and protected delivery capability. Intent/provider state cannot confirm or apply the Account change; new-address confirmation and old-address notice roles remain held in development.
Owns durable minimal evidence obligations for Account lifecycle outcomes. Audit evidence does not mutate canonical email.
Owns the operation-bound current purpose and terminal withdrawal truth. Identity reads it under the same source transaction and never copies it into Account, Session or workflow state.

ash.caller_boundary: Private Ash actions. Application callers use NewYou.Identity; Account remains the sole owner of canonical email and the current operation.
Purpose-bound proof metadata is private. Bearer values are transient and are not retained as ordinary state.
Identity establishes an intent inside its transaction; delivery and provider results are not Identity authority.

arguments: Current authenticated session credentials, requested target email, en/af locale, and caller operation UUID.
side_effects: Locks the Account, validates current session and Account posture, supersedes a prior active operation and its proof, persists the new operation and request evidence.
caller_constraints: Must be called for the currently authenticated Account; an email equal to the canonical email is unavailable.

arguments: Current session credentials, fresh password and current operation UUID.
side_effects: For a requested operation, checks current credential/security versions and purpose-bound step-up, issues a new-address confirmation proof, and records its protected Communications intent and evidence obligation. For a due confirmed operation, requires fresh password and current purpose-bound assurance, then rebinds the existing operation to the current Session without reissuing proof or changing confirmation, delay or review state.
caller_constraints: Every apply requires a current :change_primary_email Session step-up with unexpired time and matching MFA/security version bindings. Active MFA enrollment requires fresh TOTP step-up; when MFA is disabled, fresh password verification during reauthentication establishes or renews Session step-up. A new Session can be rebound only after authentication against the still-canonical old email and the same operation identity.

arguments: Transient signed confirmation bearer submitted by an explicit participant POST.
side_effects: Consumes the single-use proof and records confirmation plus the applicable apply delay/review guard; it does not update Account.email.
caller_constraints: The browser POST is CSRF protected. Passive GET/HEAD only renders a form and cannot call this interface.

returns: Applied/already-applied, terminal held/rejected outcomes, or a uniform unavailable error.
side_effects: Under the Account lock, reloads and locks the operation-bound Session and related Tokens, then rechecks operation/version identity, current Session and Token validity, purpose-bound Session step-up with MFA/security version bindings, consumed proof, delay/review, Account posture and target uniqueness. Active MFA retains its TOTP step-up; disabled MFA uses password-established Session step-up. In the development/test proof gate only, it also obtains the current Privacy-owned purpose under lock before changing the Account. Atomically applies canonical email, invalidates Sessions and Devices, establishes old-address notice intent and Audit evidence.
caller_constraints: Retries are idempotent. The apply operation and existing recovery completion serialize on the authoritative Account transaction.
The P8-17 synthetic proof purpose is development/test-only and flag-controlled; ordinary primary-email change does not require new purpose-specific consent.

arguments: Current session credentials and current operation UUID.
side_effects: Transitions the current operation to cancelled, revokes pending proof and records minimal Audit evidence.
caller_constraints: Must be performed by the Account's current authenticated Session.

request_flow.summary: Authenticated request enters Identity; Account is locked, the target is canonicalized and checked, current-operation concurrency is serialized, and a newer accepted request supersedes prior active state and proof.

Fresh password and current Session assurance are checked; every Account receives purpose-bound step-up, with active MFA requiring TOTP and disabled MFA using fresh password verification. Identity persists fixed signed claims and a Token proof while the bearer exists only for protected delivery.

Communications resolves the exact approved EN/AF development message identity. Delivery/provider execution remains held and disabled; the signed proof is exposed only through the protected transient capability.
GET/HEAD returns a no-store confirmation form without consuming proof. A CSRF-protected explicit POST consumes it once and records confirmation, leaving canonical email unchanged until apply commits.

Apply locks and rechecks current Account state and guards in a single Ash transaction. Success changes canonical email and commits Session/Device invalidation, old-address notice intent and Audit evidence; retry returns the terminal receipt.

security_invariants.summary: Account is the only canonical-email and current-operation owner. No canonical write occurs during request, proof issuance or confirmation.
Passive GET/HEAD, scanners and prefetch cannot consume proof; explicit CSRF-protected participant POST is single use and separate from apply.
Raw protected bearer is transient and excluded from ordinary persistence, logs, endpoint telemetry, jobs and Audit evidence; responses and rendered pages do not echo it after confirmation.

Final apply revalidates the persisted operation-bound Session and linked authentication Token under lock, including active state, absolute and idle deadlines, token purpose and expiry, and current :change_primary_email step-up timestamp, expiry, MFA version and security version bindings for both MFA-enabled and MFA-disabled Accounts. Logout, revocation, expiry or stale assurance denies apply without success evidence or security consequences.

Only development/test builds with the exact digest-pinned PR #229 evidence may bind the approved EN/AF messages. Production/runtime release and provider delivery remain disabled; support_contact is unbound.

concurrency.summary: Account row lock serializes operations; partial unique PostgreSQL indexes enforce one active target across Accounts and unique current operation identity at persistence boundary.

Apply and existing recovery completion operate through Identity owner interfaces in genuine competing PostgreSQL transactions. Tests prove both commit orderings and that the later stale operation cannot overwrite the winner.

Account security mutations lock Account first, related Token rows in JTI order second, then current Session rows. Primary-email apply, recovery and password reset follow this order. Tests prove logout-first denies stale apply and apply-first revokes the Session before logout can commit.
Target uniqueness and Account operation serialization are tested with real competing database transactions, including post-precheck races.

When the P8-17 development/test proof gate is enabled, Identity locks the current Privacy purpose row after its existing Account, Token and Session checks and holds that lock through the source mutation commit. Withdrawal touches only the Privacy row, so it cannot create a reverse Account/Token/Session lock order.

Separate PostgreSQL transactions prove withdrawal-first denies before mutation, while source-first obtains the Privacy lock, commits the already-authorized mutation, and allows the waiting withdrawal to commit afterwards.

idempotency_retry.summary: Operation ID and persisted Account version bind request and transitions; repeated request, confirmation, apply, cancellation or expiry does not repeat completed consequences and returns stable terminal receipts where supported.
Account, proof revocation, Communications intents and Audit obligations are composed within the owner Ash transaction so a failed write rolls back the authoritative change and can be retried.
A withdrawn proof purpose is terminal in Privacy. Identity's denied retry re-reads the owner row; it cannot restore the prior positive decision from Session or workflow state.

failure_recovery.summary: Expiry is derived from persisted deadlines and bounded batch reconciliation; it can resume after restart and revokes any pending proof.
A fresh BEAM process resumes a persisted confirmed operation and applies it through the normal guarded interface; restart proof retains only test-controlled transient proof input.

A due, confirmed operation can regain fresh assurance after a five-minute step-up expires: reauthenticate a current Session with the unchanged canonical email and fresh password, complete fresh purpose-bound TOTP step-up when MFA is active, then use the existing reauthentication interface. When MFA is disabled, that interface writes a new :change_primary_email Session step-up bound to current Account MFA/security versions after fresh password verification. The same operation, consumed proof, confirmation history, delay and review state remain in place; no duplicate proof is issued, and apply remains blocked until all original guards pass.

When the old address is inaccessible, participant enters existing governed recovery interfaces. Recovery completion invalidates primary-email-change authority and serializes with apply; no support-note or Communications state changes canonical email.

Missing, withdrawn or unavailable current Privacy authority fails closed in the proof gate. Retry after withdrawal and a fresh BEAM restart remain denied; Privacy keeps the current durable state and append-only transition evidence.

safe_extensions.summary: Future production eligibility requires new explicit durable authority and verified content/provider approval; current development eligibility must remain off by default.
An approved policy may supply delay and review requirements through the existing Identity guard seam without moving canonical authority out of Account.

reuse.summary: Reuse the existing Account, Session, DeviceAssurance, Token proof, Communications protected delivery and disposition, Audit E2 evidence, and governed recovery interfaces.
Reuse exact approved EN/AF message identities and the PR #229 development evidence packet; do not alter content or bind support_contact.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Do not make browser GET/HEAD, scanner/prefetch, Communications provider success, Audit evidence, cached/browser state or support notes consume proof or mutate canonical email.
Do not create another canonical email owner or call Account resource actions directly from controllers/workers; application writes use Identity interfaces.
Do not persist/log raw proof or enable provider, production, runtime release or real-participant delivery under this development-only capability.

proof_limitations: The full local mix check and focused tests are author-side evidence; exact-head CI and independent Master Gate review are still required.
Restart recovery is proven with the existing test harness and a fresh BEAM process against the isolated test database; it is not a production deployment test.
Session/logout and recovery/apply contention proof uses independent PostgreSQL transactions in the local test database; it does not model cross-region or production database failure modes.
Delay and risk-review policy exercised by development tests does not select production thresholds or authorize live participant delivery.
Selected E2 records carry minimal event facts only; they do not contain bearer proof or full private diagnostics.
